correctness.rationale: The induction c a_W c=a_W c combines with a_i c a_i=a_i c to produce a_S or a_U c a_V with disjoint U,V. Sending all leaves but one to 1 preserves the relations. The five transformations 1,a,c,ac,ca check the two-letter quotient, and the resulting projection tuple is injective since it recovers the normal-form type and all leaf states (m≥1). The image is the union of the two full cubes {1,a}^m and {c,ac,ca}^m. On one coordinate the leaf–leaf block has four ordered commuting pairs, either mixed block has four, and the hub–hub block has seven (only c and ca fail to commute with each other). The row counts in these blocks produce the two centralizer sizes for each element and sum to 7^m+3·4^m. Only 1 and the full-leaf form followed by c use entirely universal rows in their respective blocks. Division by (2^m+3^m)^2 gives the equivalent (7/9)^m. The source checker and its stored finite m=1,…,5 outputs were inspected, not replayed; the proof is valid at arbitrary positive m.

originality.rationale: The size, normal-form shape, and commutation test restricted to idempotents have prior coverage and are not credited as new. The supported distinct result is the element-wise centralizer spectrum and resulting all-element commuting law for the Hecke–Kiselman star. The strongest different record gives a nearly parallel formula for a star left regular band but different hub centralizers, while the closest same-monoid prior record analyzes only idempotent commutation for its endomorphism calculation. Deriving the full spectrum needs identifying the faithful coordinate model and evaluating the local non-idempotent commutation block, not substituting m into those results.
residual_risks: An equivalent edge-quotient centralizer formula might exist under other Kiselman/Catalan terminology or in uncatalogued work. The assessment is about verified mathematical coverage, not historical priority.

value.rationale: For a canonical noncommutative graph family, the full centralizer invariant and asymptotic describe all elements rather than the idempotent subfamily. The two-cube representation accounts for the growth constant and explains why an equally large star dependence band has different commutation statistics.
